wsl-claude, for 'refactor our app plugin-model': what the tree has today (6630efb), read only, nothing built. FIVE kinds of 'app', each wired differently:
1) PAGE APPS in app/<name>/ (most of the 20: apps, files, jobs, natter, desk...). A manifest, a page, the shell hosts them.
2) BOOTED FACELESS APPS, 'boots': true (appFaceApp, fixList), run INSIDE the node by nodeApps.mountAll, with an api object and an allow.json list.
3) FACE-SERVED APPS, 'serves': true plus a contract ('surface', 'utilities', 'posture', 'refusals': faceProof, and starter with the contract but no 'serves'), run as a faceServer process.
4) PROCESS JOBS in spirit/run/process/js/<name>/ (14: agents, imageCaption*, localReview, wordpressScanner...): a separate folder, no manifest, they require kernel.js and report through the callback URL.
5) PERMANENT JOBS written into the core (fs-watcher, server-stats).
And manifest flags that each mean a different mechanism: boots, serves, listens (desk), type (the *Details panes), handlesExtensions (textEditor), intrinsic, hidden, owner, plus the contract fields.
So the smell: five homes, two folders, ~10 flags, and no single place that says what an app IS or what it may reach. A plugin model would be one manifest shape that declares which of those faces an app has (page, faceless-in-node, server process, job), and one loader that reads it.
